question: How to Calculate Symmetrical and Asymmetrical Short Circuit Current?
body_html:
Short circuit current calculation to IEC 60909 starts with the symmetrical RMS value, then adds the decaying DC offset to get the asymmetrical peak.

Symmetrical: I″k = c × Vn / (√3 × Zk). Example: 1.05 × 400 V / (1.732 × 0.01 Ω) ≈ 24.2 kA.

Peak asymmetrical: ip = κ × √2 × I″k. With κ = 1.8, ip ≈ 61.6 kA.

Breaker interrupting ratings use symmetrical RMS current, while busbar and switchgear withstand ratings use the peak.
